summary:
The core of the design is sound. It recounts the facts, twinned and pattern figures from the tree's own yaml and .cs, independently of eng/rules-parity.ps1, then adds measured per-site offsets. The committed SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified forces this over read-back, so leaving the brief's wording is justified. Both cited sources say what the design claims they say.

Four places still depend on people remembering, or give a check that passes for the wrong reason:
1. Format-AgreeLine accepts absolute counts, and none of the five guard regexes catches a literal passed to it. The guard also misses the C-007 'xunit 11 Facts' literal that the design's own case says it must hit, and no committed test proves the new rule fires.
2. A recount failure thrown under -File exits 1 on PowerShell 5 and later, the same code as 'N check(s) failed'. If the Misclassified probe's scratch tree has no ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, which C-001 never needed before, the probe passes without testing anything. That leaves the must-verify 'a miscounting tool still fails C-001' unchecked.
3. C-007 and C-008, the least-verified sites, may be skipped under 'or record that they were not run'.
4. The repro is committed unchanged and sits outside the guard's scope. If it pins 12/16/28 or '47 settled', this slice's own settled entry (fitness.yaml is already modified in the worktree) or the next twinned slice brings the same bug back in a new file.

Nothing here blocks the slice. Each fix is local.

Four places still depend on people remembering, or give a check that passes for the wrong reason:
1. Format-AgreeLine accepts absolute counts, and none of the five guard regexes catches a literal passed to it. The guard also misses the C-007 'xunit 11 Facts' literal that the design's own case says it must hit, and no committed test proves the new rule fires.
2. A recount failure thrown under -File exits 1 on PowerShell 5 and later, the same code as 'N check(s) failed'. findings.claim: The rule 'expectations are always clean-recount + offset, never an absolute count' depends on each call site remembering it. Format-AgreeLine takes absolute -Facts/-Twinned/-Patterns parameters, and Get-RuleCounts takes a -Repo path. A later site can write `Format-AgreeLine -Facts 12 -Twinned 16 -Patterns 28 -Settled (...)`, `$Facts = 11`, `Patterns = 27`, or `Get-RuleCounts -Repo $fixture`, which is the mutated-fixture recount the design explicitly rejects. None of the five must_not_match regexes (`AGREE \d+ facts`, `<- \d+ twinned`, `\d+ patterns;`, `-ExpectFacts\s+['"]?\d`, `\bTwinned\s*=\s*\d`) matches any of these. The design's new API is itself the way past the guard.
findings.evidence: components 'Format-AgreeLine' ('Format-AgreeLine -Facts -Twinned -Patterns -Settled -> string'), 'Get-RuleCounts -Repo <path>'; architecture_rules must_not_match list; key decision 'Recount the clean $Repo once ... Do not recount each mutated fixture'
findings.fix: Make the invariant impossible to break. Format-AgreeLine (and a matching ExpectFacts helper) should take only offsets (-DFacts/-DTwinned/-DPatterns, default 0) and read $script:Counts itself, with Settled always from Get-ExpectedSettled. Get-RuleCounts should take no path and be called once on the script's own absolute $Repo. As a backstop, add `-(Facts|Twinned|Patterns)\s+\d` and `\b(Facts|Patterns)\s*=\s*\d` to must_not_match.

findings.claim: The guard rule does not cover every literal the design lists, and nothing committed proves that it fires. The design's case says the guard must hit HEAD's RuleCases.ps1 at line 600 ('xunit 11 Facts'), but no regex matches `xunit \d+ Facts`. C-005's message 'the reader found 11 Facts where the test class has 12' is also unmatched unless `-ExpectFacts 12` happens to be on the same line. SL-053's equivalent rule has a committed behavioural check (SettledCountProbe -Shape GuardRule). The new rule gets only an ad-hoc 'plus Select-String' at build time, so a regex that matches nothing, which the design itself calls 'worthless', would ship.
findings.evidence: cases: 'literal-count guard rule ... HEAD's RuleCases.ps1 (literals at lines 35, 238/240, 243, 305, 326, 370, 408, 600, 625, 633)'; survey evidence: "C-007 'xunit 11 Facts' (600)", "'the reader found 11 Facts where the test class has 12' with `-ExpectFacts 12` (370)"
findings.fix: Add `xunit \d+ Facts` and `found \d+ Facts where the test class has \d+` to must_not_match. Add a committed check, either a new SettledCountProbe shape or a step in the sibling test, that runs the rule's regexes against a pinned pre-fix copy (git show a9e0d1d:tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1), requires a hit on every listed line, and requires zero hits on the working file.

findings.claim: A recount failure can't be told apart from a caught miscount, so the must-verify 'a miscounting tool still fails C-001' can pass without testing anything. The contract says Get-RuleCounts throws and the script exits non-zero. Under -File on PowerShell 5 and later an uncaught throw exits 1, the same code as 'N check(s) failed.' The Misclassified shape passes when C-001 fails. Its scratch tree swaps in a stub parity tool, and until now C-001 read only the yaml (Get-ExpectedSettled), so nobody has checked that the probe copies ArchitectureRulesTests.cs. If it doesn't, the recount throws 'missing file', C-001 exits 1, and the probe goes green whatever the counting logic does. The design checks this precondition only as 'must still exit 0'.
findings.evidence: contract Get-RuleCounts error_cases 'The script exits non-zero before any case runs'; cross_domain_transfer must-verify 'A miscounting tool still fails C-001 ... It must still exit 0 after the change'. Exit code on throw: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28724388 ('With Powershell 5 and up: When an exception is thrown, exit code defaults to 1'). about_Throw (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_throw) notes that $ErrorActionPreference SilentlyContinue/Ignore suppresses throw entirely.
findings.fix: In the main block, catch the recount failure and `exit 3` with the reason, rather than letting a bare throw produce exit 1. When checking Misclassified after the change, require that C-001 exits 1 (not 3) and that its output contains the FAIL row for the twinned mismatch (expected 15, stub 14). Also confirm that SettledCountProbe.ps1 copies ArchitectureRulesTests.cs into its scratch tree. To settle it: run `SettledCountProbe.ps1 -Shape Misclassified` with the child's stdout captured, and grep for the twinned FAIL row.

findings.claim: The C-007 and C-008 rewrites (lines 600, 625, 633) and the C-008 Twinned-1 offset are the only sites nobody has run. The survey and spikes had no engine, and the lockstep spike only reproduced the mutation's parity line. Yet the design lets build skip them: 'Build must run them with -EnginePython/-EngineRoot, or record that they were not run.' The brief's criterion is that rule-copy cases stay green, and C-008 is one of those cases. The engine's own interpreter is available to the stage that runs the build, so skipping is a choice, not a limitation.
findings.evidence: coherence_check 'What no stage settled: C-006..C-014 need the TAAD engine ... Build must run them ... or record that they were not run'; case 'C-008 tests-scope entry deleted ... this is unverified until run with the engine'; sibling test 'C-007 and C-008 run in it only when -EnginePython/-EngineRoot are supplied'
findings.fix: Make it a required build/validate check to run `RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-007` and `-Case C-008` with -EnginePython/-EngineRoot on the clean tree and on at least the two-scope scratch variant, under both hosts. If they cannot be run, the stage is not-reached, not passed.

findings.claim: The committed repro (and the new sibling test) could carry the very bug this slice removes. The design commits tests/bugs/SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts.Tests.ps1 'unchanged', and the guard's `files` covers only tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1. The repro's setup guard 'AGREEd on the scratch tree at 12/16/28'. If it checks that line literally, the next twinned slice turns the committed regression test red. If it pins '47 settled', it breaks now: the worktree already shows `M .taad/fitness.yaml`, and the design's new settled entry moves the real tree to 48. The sibling test is specified to build 'the same kind of scratch tree', which invites the same literals.
findings.evidence: component 'Committed repro: Commit the untracked tests/bugs/SL-069-RuleCasesDeriveCounts.Tests.ps1 unchanged'; architecture_rules files: 'tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1'; repro account 'the parity tool AGREEd on the scratch tree at 12/16/28'; git status 'M .taad/fitness.yaml'
findings.fix: Before committing, run `Select-String tests/bugs/SL-069-*.ps1 -Pattern '\b(1[1256]|2[78]|4[78])\b'`, then re-run the repro against the current (modified) fitness.yaml. Require both scratch tests to take their expected parity line from the clean tree's line plus the added delta, and extend the guard's `files` to tests/bugs/SL-069-*.ps1. If the repro really cannot be edited and it pins counts, raise that with the repro stage now.

findings.claim: The design leaves the engine-written fitness rule conditional ('If the engine also writes architecture_rules into the registry, build must not add a second copy'), but the tree shows it has happened. The build check saw a clean status; the worktree now has `M .taad/fitness.yaml`. Twinned is defined by position (entries above the FIRST '# settled by SL-' marker). An entry the engine inserted above that marker, or without the '  # settled by SL-069' marker the design specifies, counts as a 16th twinned entry with no Fact. Parity then DRIFTs, and C-001 goes red on the clean tree.
findings.evidence: component 'Literal-parity-count guard (fitness rule)' key_interactions; git status snapshot 'M .taad/fitness.yaml' vs build-check 'git status --short shows only .taad/slices/SL-069/ and the repro test as untracked'
findings.fix: Make this build's first step: run `git diff -- .taad/fitness.yaml`, keep exactly one copy placed below the last settled block under '  # settled by SL-069', then require eng/rules-parity.ps1 to print AGREE 11/15/27/48 on the real tree.

findings.claim: The pattern regex `^\s*@".*"\s*(,|\);)\s*$` counts every line that consists only of a verbatim string. Parity counts Fact patterns. They agree only because of the current .cs style, and nobody has checked that against the repro's inserted Fact. If the repro writes its new pattern inline (e.g. `Check(@"x");`), with a trailing comment, or in non-verbatim form, the recount gives 27 while parity gives 28. The acceptance test then fails, and because the repro cannot change, the recount has to widen. The design's case against circularity applies to Facts (-ExpectFacts), not to patterns, so there is no reason for the pattern definition to differ from the reader's.
findings.evidence: component Get-RuleCounts 'Patterns = lines matching ...'; must-verify 'The recount moves with a twinned-rule addition (12/16/28 on the repro's scratch tree ...)'; spike measured the recount only on the clean tree
findings.fix: Before rewiring any case, run the three recount regexes against the repro's generated scratch .cs and both sibling variants, and require 12/16/28 (and the two-scope figures). State in the design that the pattern definition deliberately follows the parity reader's.

findings.claim: The loose Fact regex has not been measured, and the design has no route if it gives more than 11 on the clean tree. C-001 would then pass -ExpectFacts 12 and the reader would return CANNOT-READ, turning the clean tree red. The design says 'report, don't narrow', but the fix would be in eng/rules-parity.ps1, outside this slice, so the slice would be blocked mid-build.
findings.evidence: key decision 'The recount's Fact regex is looser ... If the looser regex yields more than 11 on the clean tree, that is a real reader gap to report'; must-verify 'The loose Fact regex yields 11 on the clean tree'
findings.fix: Make the first build step `Select-String -Path tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs -Pattern '^\s*\[\s*(Fact|Theory)\b'`. If it returns anything other than 11, stop and send the reader gap back before writing any code.

findings.claim: Get-RuleCounts reads with [IO.File]::ReadAllLines under a public -Repo parameter. .NET BCL methods resolve relative paths against the process's working directory, not PowerShell's $PWD. A relative -Repo, or a caller that changes location with Set-Location, would read the wrong tree or throw 'missing file'. This is another rule that depends on remembering.
findings.evidence: component Get-RuleCounts 'Lines are read with [IO.File]::ReadAllLines'; https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/3428 (Resolution-By Design: '.NET methods: $pwd is _not_ honored')
findings.fix: Drop the -Repo parameter as in M1, or normalise it inside the function with `Convert-Path`/`(Resolve-Path $Repo).ProviderPath` before any [IO.File] call.

findings.claim: Several of the design's own cases have no named test. These are: Get-RuleCounts with no marker, with a missing .cs, or with a zero count; a yaml with more than one settled marker; and a Fact the reader cannot see (`[Fact(Skip=...)]`, `[Fact, Trait(...)]`). The sibling test runs only two positive variants, so the fail-before-any-case contract and the loose-regex behaviour could ship unexercised.
findings.evidence: cases 'Get-RuleCounts on unreadable input' (x2), 'Get-RuleCounts on a yaml with more than one settled marker', 'C-001 with a Fact the parity reader cannot see'; component 'Every-case-follows-counts sibling test' (two variants only)
findings.fix: Add three scratch variants to the sibling test: the marker removed (expect the distinct recount exit code from M3 before any case row), the .cs deleted (same), and one `[Fact(Skip="x")]` added with no twin (expect C-001 exit 1).

findings.claim: The open question gets the timing of the SettledCountProbe.ps1:125 residual wrong. The stub's literal line (14 twinned / 48 settled) goes stale in THIS slice, not 'after the next twinned slice'. This slice's settled entry moves the real tree to 15/48, so a true misclassification would read 14/49. The probe still turns C-001 red on the twinned mismatch, so it isn't inverted, but it now fails for a mixed reason from the moment this slice merges. Keeping the recount inside RuleCases.ps1 also means the follow-up can't reuse it.
findings.evidence: open_questions 'after the next twinned slice it can no longer tell a real misclassification from a stale stub line'; build-check 'moves one twinned entry to settled (14 twinned, 48 settled)'; component 'Literal-parity-count guard' 'Moves the real tree's settled count from 47 to 48'
findings.fix: Correct the open question to say the stub is stale on merge. Either derive line 125 from the yaml in this slice (a single line, in the same way as Get-ExpectedSettled) or file the follow-up now against SL-069 rather than 'the next twinned slice'.

dimensions_checked.result: M5 (the committed repro and sibling test may pin counts; outside the guard's scope) and m2 (the pattern regex is unverified against the repro's inserted Fact). Must-verify '$Repo resolves to the scratch root' is effectively settled by the captured repro output: the scratch copy's C-001 printed parity's 12/16/28 line, so it ran against the scratch tree. The yaml and .cs must be there because the setup guard's parity run read them. Cited prior art checked: goldenmatch emit_ts_parity_fixtures.py does say it 'deliberately emit[s] only the invariants that survive the skew' from a separate Python implementation, and parallax case_runner.py does assert 'the number of golden SQL statements equals the declared roundTrips' and exec(referenceSql) == rows. Both support the design's claims. The recalled items (Jest -u, Weyuker) are decorative, not load-bearing, and were left unchecked.

m3 (the loose Fact regex could exceed 11 on the clean tree, with no route to handle it) and m6 (the stub literal goes stale in this slice). Two-scope Facts, multiple settled markers, BOM and C-005's N+1 are all covered by the design's cases.
Covered by M1: the absolute-count parameters on Format-AgreeLine and Get-RuleCounts -Repo leave the offset-only rule dependent on each call site remembering it.
none: Format-AgreeLine, count-free titles, the one settled guard rule and the two-variant sibling test each answer a stale site or a measured shape (SL-043's two-scope move). Nothing is speculative.

The M3 exit-code collision (recount failure = exit 1 = checks failed) is a gap in the CLI contract. The Format-AgreeLine contract ties itself to rules-parity's wording by remembering, but a wording change fails loudly on every case, so that is acceptable.

M3 (a throw under -File exits 1, so the Misclassified probe can pass without testing anything; about_Throw also notes that SilentlyContinue suppresses throw) and m4 (ReadAllLines ignores $PWD for relative paths, per PowerShell#3428, By Design).

The move from 'read the numbers from the parity output' to an independent recount is justified. Read-back would make C-001 agree with the stub tool, and the committed SettledCountProbe -Shape Misclassified would go red. The existing probe settles that decidable disagreement; it does not need a new tournament. m1: the tree shows fitness.yaml already modified, while the design treats that as hypothetical.
M1: the guard's must_not_match list is written against today's string spelling, not against the API the design introduces. M2: it also misses the existing C-007/C-005 literals.
M2 (no committed proof that the new guard fires, and line 600 is not matched), M4 (C-007/C-008 may be skipped) and m5 (error-path and blind-spot cases have no test).
none: local test scripts reading repo files. No external input, credentials, network or elevation.
